conflicts.fact: Runner B's velocity during the slow middle section of the marathon
conflicts.versions: Lesson 2 and Lesson 7's overview/explanation give about 17.6 km/h for 25–35 km. Lesson 5 gives 5.6 m/s (about 20 km/h) falling to 4.9 m/s (17.6 km/h). Lesson 7's model-building phase gives Runner B at 17 km/h.

Lesson 2 says about 22 km/h; Lesson 5 says 6.2 m/s (about 22.3 km/h), which is consistent; but Lesson 7's model-building phase has Runner A at 21 km/h, a different value from the roughly 19 km/h constant pace in Lessons 1 and 2.

Lessons 1 and 2 and the Lesson 7 explanation give about 19 km/h, nearly constant. The Lesson 7 model-building phase gives Runner A at 21 km/h (relative speed 21 − 17 = 4 km/h) while the same lesson's explanation gives 19 − 17.6 = 1.4 km/h.

conflicts.fact: Overtake time and relative speed between Runner A and Runner B
conflicts.versions: The explanation says a 200 m gap at 1.4 km/h takes about 8.6 minutes. The model-building phase uses a relative speed of 4 km/h with the same 200 m gap, which gives 3 minutes. The overtake is also placed in the slow section (25–35 km) in one place and 'about 4 km to go' in the other.

conflicts.fact: When and where Runner A overtook Runner B
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 says Runner B was ahead at 30 km. Lesson 3 says Runner A overtook during 30–35 km. Lesson 6 says Runner A overtook within the 25–35 km segment. Lesson 7's model has the overtake with about 4 km to go (around 38 km), which conflicts with the 25–35 km slow section.

conflicts.fact: Which lessons built which graphs, and the earlier graph types
conflicts.versions: Lesson 6 says displacement-time graphs and speed calculations were added in Lessons 4–5 and speaks of a distance-time graph. In the sequence, displacement-time graphs were drawn in Lesson 3 and the velocity-time graph in Lesson 5.

conflicts.fact: Class race interval and data recorded
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 Observed says the class recorded split times at 10 m intervals over 40 m and 80 m distances. Lesson 1 Model Building describes only a 40 m course. Lesson 1's Overview mentions both 40 m and 80 m.

conflicts.fact: Which runner's speed was calculated and how
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 says Runner A's average speed is about 19 km/h. Lesson 2's Explain section says acceleration units are 'm/s² or km/h/s', while the Observe section works in km/h per segment; the Lesson 2 summary also calls velocity 's/t' with s as displacement, while speed in Lesson 1 is distance ÷ time.
